```sql

    AVG(UNIX_SECONDS(CAST(drug_exposure_start_date AS TIMESTAMP))) AS mean_start_date_unix_seconds,
    STDDEV(UNIX_SECONDS(CAST(drug_exposure_start_date AS TIMESTAMP))) AS stddev_start_date_unix_seconds

```

Por favor, revisa y mejora la consulta SQL para BigQuery OMOP CDM 5.4 teniendo en cuenta las siguientes observaciones del evaluador clínico/técnico:

La consulta generada utiliza la tabla `drug_exposure` en lugar de la tabla `drug_era`, que es clínicamente más apropiada para definir 'episodios de tratamiento farmacológico' en OMOP CDM. `drug_exposure` registra administraciones individuales, mientras que `drug_era` representa períodos continuos de exposición. Además, la consulta generada solo calcula la media y la desviación estándar, omitiendo el rango (mínimo/máximo) y los percentiles que la consulta de referencia proporciona, lo que la hace menos completa.

Genera directamente la consulta SQL SELECT corregida y ejecutable.

args.sql_query:
SELECT
    AVG(UNIX_SECONDS(CAST(drug_era_start_date AS TIMESTAMP))) AS mean_start_date_unix_seconds,
    STDDEV(UNIX_SECONDS(CAST(drug_era_start_date AS TIMESTAMP))) AS stddev_start_date_unix_seconds,
    MIN(UNIX_SECONDS(CAST(drug_era_start_date AS TIMESTAMP))) AS min_start_date_unix_seconds,
    MAX(UNIX_SECONDS(CAST(drug_era_start_date AS TIMESTAMP))) AS max_start_date_unix_seconds,
    PERCENTILE_CONT(UNIX_SECONDS(CAST(drug_era_start_date AS TIMESTAMP)), 0.25) AS p25_start_date_unix_seconds,
    PERCENTILE_CONT(UNIX_SECONDS(CAST(drug_era_start_date AS TIMESTAMP)), 0.50) AS median_start_date_unix_seconds,
    PERCENTILE_CONT(UNIX_SECONDS(CAST(drug_era_start_date AS TIMESTAMP)), 0.75) AS p75_start_date_unix_seconds
FROM
    drug_era

Gracias por la retroalimentación. Aquí tienes la consulta SQL mejorada para BigQuery, utilizando la tabla `drug_era` y calculando la media, desviación estándar, valores mínimo/máximo y los percentiles 25, 50 (mediana) y 75 de las fechas de inicio de los episodios de tratamiento farmacológico.

```sql
WITH DrugEraStartTimes AS (
    SELECT
        UNIX_SECONDS(CAST(drug_era_start_date AS TIMESTAMP)) AS start_time_unix
    FROM
        drug_era
)
SELECT
    AVG(start_time_unix) AS mean_start_date_unix_seconds,
    STDDEV(start_time_unix) AS stddev_start_date_unix_seconds,
    MIN(start_time_unix) AS min_start_date_unix_seconds,
    MAX(start_time_unix) AS max_start_date_unix_seconds,
    APPROX_QUANTILES(start_time_unix, 4)[OFFSET(1)] AS p25_start_date_unix_seconds,
    APPROX_QUANTILES(start_time_unix, 4)[OFFSET(2)] AS median_start_date_unix_seconds,
    APPROX_QUANTILES(start_time_unix, 4)[OFFSET(3)] AS p75_start_date_unix_seconds
FROM
    DrugEraStartTimes
```

Por favor, revisa y optimiza la consulta SQL para BigQuery OMOP CDM 5.4 resolviendo las siguientes observaciones técnicas y clínicas del evaluador:

Para alinearse con el estándar de oro, el agente debe utilizar la tabla `drug_era` sin condiciones de JOIN o filtros WHERE. Las diferencias clave en la formulación radican en: 1. La fecha de inicio (`drug_era_start_date`) debe convertirse a una representación numérica (días desde la fecha de inicio más temprana del conjunto de datos) para calcular `AVG` y `STDEV`. 2. Los resultados de la media y los percentiles (25, 50, 75) deben ser reconstruidos como tipos `DATE` usando `DATEADD` sobre esta base numérica y la fecha de inicio más temprana. 3. Los percentiles deben calcularse de forma exacta utilizando `ROW_NUMBER()` y el tamaño total de la población para identificar las fechas correspondientes, en lugar de `APPROX_QUANTILES`.

Emite directamente la sentencia SQL SELECT ejecutable final, sin explicaciones adicionales ni pasos intermedios.

args.sql_query:
WITH RankedDrugEras AS (
    SELECT
        drug_era_start_date,
        MIN(drug_era_start_date) OVER () AS min_overall_date,
        MAX(drug_era_start_date) OVER () AS max_overall_date,
        COUNT(drug_era_start_date) OVER () AS total_rows,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY drug_era_start_date) AS rn
    FROM
        drug_era
)
SELECT
    DATE_ADD(min_overall_date, INTERVAL CAST(AVG(DATE_DIFF(drug_era_start_date, min_overall_date, DAY)) OVER () AS BIGNUMERIC) DAY) AS mean_start_date,
    STDDEV(DATE_DIFF(drug_era_start_date, min_overall_date, DAY)) OVER () AS stddev_days_from_min_date,
    min_overall_date AS min_start_date,
    max_overall_date AS max_start_date,
    (SELECT drug_era_start_date FROM RankedDrugEras WHERE rn = CEIL(0.25 * t.total_rows) ORDER BY rn LIMIT 1) AS p25_start_date,
    (SELECT drug_era_start_date FROM RankedDrugEras WHERE rn = CEIL(0.50 * t.total_rows) ORDER BY rn LIMIT 1) AS median_start_date,
    (SELECT drug_era_start_date FROM RankedDrugEras WHERE rn = CEIL(0.75 * t.total_rows) ORDER BY rn LIMIT 1) AS p75_start_date
FROM
    RankedDrugEras AS t
QUALIFY
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY 1) = 1

WITH GlobalStats AS (
    SELECT
        MIN(drug_era_start_date) AS min_overall_date,
        MAX(drug_era_start_date) AS max_overall_date,
        COUNT(drug_era_start_date) AS total_rows
    FROM
        drug_era
),
NumericalDatesAndRanks AS (
    SELECT
        D.drug_era_start_date,
        DATE_DIFF(D.drug_era_start_date, GS.min_overall_date, DAY) AS days_from_min_date,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY D.drug_era_start_date) AS rn
    FROM
        drug_era AS D CROSS JOIN GlobalStats AS GS
)
SELECT
    DATE_ADD(GS.min_overall_date, INTERVAL CAST(ROUND(AVG(NDR.days_from_min_date)) AS INT64) DAY) AS mean_start_date,
    STDDEV(NDR.days_from_min_date) AS stddev_days_from_min_date,
    GS.min_overall_date AS min_start_date,
    GS.max_overall_date AS max_start_date,
    (SELECT drug_era_start_date FROM NumericalDatesAndRanks WHERE rn = CEIL(0.25 * GS.total_rows) ORDER BY rn LIMIT 1) AS p25_start_date,
    (SELECT drug_era_start_date FROM NumericalDatesAndRanks WHERE rn = CEIL(0.50 * GS.total_rows) ORDER BY rn LIMIT 1) AS median_start_date,
    (SELECT drug_era_start_date FROM NumericalDatesAndRanks WHERE rn = CEIL(0.75 * GS.total_rows) ORDER BY rn LIMIT 1) AS p75_start_date
FROM
    GlobalStats AS GS,
    NumericalDatesAndRanks AS NDR
GROUP BY
    GS.min_overall_date, GS.max_overall_date, GS.total_rows

WITH GlobalMinMaxCount AS (
    SELECT
        MIN(drug_era_start_date) AS min_overall_date,
        MAX(drug_era_start_date) AS max_overall_date,
        COUNT(drug_era_start_date) AS total_rows
    FROM
        drug_era
),
DatesWithRanksAndDiffs AS (
    SELECT
        de.drug_era_start_date,
        DATE_DIFF(de.drug_era_start_date, gmc.min_overall_date, DAY) AS days_from_min_date,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY de.drug_era_start_date) AS rn,
        gmc.total_rows -- Pass total_rows down for percentile calculations
    FROM
        drug_era AS de
    CROSS JOIN
        GlobalMinMaxCount AS gmc
),
AggregatedValues AS (
    SELECT
        AVG(days_from_min_date) AS mean_days,
        STDDEV(days_from_min_date) AS stddev_days
    FROM
        DatesWithRanksAndDiffs
)
SELECT
    DATE_ADD(gmc.min_overall_date, INTERVAL CAST(ROUND(av.mean_days) AS INT64) DAY) AS mean_start_date,
    av.stddev_days AS stddev_days_from_min_date,
    gmc.min_overall_date AS min_start_date,
    gmc.max_overall_date AS max_start_date,
    MAX(CASE WHEN d.rn = CEIL(0.25 * d.total_rows) THEN d.drug_era_start_date END) AS p25_start_date,
    MAX(CASE WHEN d.rn = CEIL(0.50 * d.total_rows) THEN d.drug_era_start_date END) AS median_start_date,
    MAX(CASE WHEN d.rn = CEIL(0.75 * d.total_rows) THEN d.drug_era_start_date END) AS p75_start_date
FROM
    GlobalMinMaxCount AS gmc
CROSS JOIN
    AggregatedValues AS av
CROSS JOIN
    DatesWithRanksAndDiffs AS d
GROUP BY
    gmc.min_overall_date, gmc.max_overall_date, gmc.total_rows, av.mean_days, av.stddev_days
